item.title: Greenlight Financial’s Luna AI automates 90% of security triage using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description:
Greenlight Financial’s Luna AI automates 90% of security triage using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

Greenlight Financial has updated its Luna AI platform to automatically resolve more than 90 % of up to 4,000 security and risk cases each month, relying on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for the underlying agent infrastructure.

🔍 Overview

  • The Security Operations Center (SOC) receives 3,000–4,000 alerts per month from four primary vectors: dark‑web breach cards, identity and access anomalies, infrastructure alerts, and financial‑risk events.
  • Each alert historically required a human analyst 15–30 minutes to cross‑reference multiple data sources.
  • Luna now handles the bulk of triage without human intervention, reducing the median triage time for routine cases to single‑digit seconds.

🧩 How it works

  • Luna is built as a hierarchical, tiered‑supervisor multi‑agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
  • AgentCore runtime hosts Luna’s agent code; AgentCore memory supports the tiered structure, eliminating the need to build these capabilities in‑house.
  • Tier 1 supervisor runs an advanced language model on Amazon Bedrock within a private VPC, orchestrating more than 30 specialized agents.
  • Incoming cases reach Tier 1 via two paths:
    • Amazon API Gateway exposing the Luna Queue API and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint.
    • Tines SOAR for automated alert ingestion.
  • Tier 1 determines the appropriate specialized agents, synthesizes findings, and issues a verdict.
  • Cases that exceed Tier 1’s confidence threshold are escalated to a Tier 2 supervisor that uses an advanced foundation model with extended reasoning capabilities. Tier 2:
    • Invokes specialized agents through boto3 with expanded context windows.
    • Chains reasoning across 3–5 data sources to establish causality.
    • Produces detailed investigation reports with evidence chains for human review.
  • Different teams can engage Luna through three entry points, ranging from fully automated ingestion to interactive on‑demand investigation.

⚙️ Key details

Alert Vector What the alert signals
Dark web breach cards Card Network and internal threat intel flag Greenlight customer cards found on the dark web
Identity and access anomalies Unusual login patterns, privilege escalations, and policy violations across IdP and internal systems
Infrastructure alerts Signals from EDR, SIEM, Asset Inventory, and other observability tools
Financial risk events Suspicious transaction patterns, compliance triggers, and fraud indicators from card processing systems
  • AgentCore memory enables the tiered multi‑agent system.
  • The runtime operates in private subnets with code deployed via a ZIP file and Amazon S3.
  • Luna triages dark‑web breach‑card alerts, identity anomalies, and financial‑risk events in seconds.

🚀 Impact

  • >90 % of up to 4,000 monthly cases are resolved without human input.
  • Human analysts are freed from the 15‑30 minute per‑case workflow, allowing focus on the remaining ~10 % of cases that require multi‑step reasoning.
  • The architecture mirrors traditional SOC team hierarchies while delivering single‑digit‑second median triage times for routine alerts.

📡 Integration points

  • Amazon API Gateway: exposes Luna Queue API and Model Context Protocol endpoint.
  • Tines SOAR: provides automated alert ingestion.
  • boto3: used by Tier 2 supervisor to call specialized agents with expanded context.

#AIagents #SecurityAutomation #AmazonBedrock

Source: How Greenlight Financial built an autonomous SOC solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Open‑Source AI Security Operations Center (AiSOC) Enables Self‑Hosted Threat Detection
item.description:
Open‑Source AI Security Operations Center (AiSOC) Enables Self‑Hosted Threat Detection

An open‑source AI Security Operations Center called AiSOC has been released. It runs on‑premises, requires no external API keys, and provides end‑to‑end alert fusion, automated triage, and auditable AI‑driven investigation.

🔍 Overview

  • Self‑hostable AI SOC licensed under MIT.
  • Ingests security telemetry from existing tools.
  • Detects, correlates, and investigates threats with LLM agents.
  • Every agent step is recorded in a replayable decision ledger.

🧩 How it works

  • Telemetry arrives from your security tools and is normalized by AiSOC.
  • The platform runs 2,966 executable rules from a 7,407‑rule library to fire alerts.
  • Fired alerts are grouped into incidents and handed to an AI agent.
  • The agent’s prompts, tool calls, and reasoning are fully auditable.
  • After investigation the agent proposes a response that a human must approve.
  • New threat‑intelligence data (e.g., the CISA KEV catalog) re‑sweeps historical data, again requiring human approval before any vendor interaction.

⚙️ Key details

  • Alert fusion, LLM‑agent triage, MITRE ATT&CK investigation.
  • Replayable decision ledger for every agent step.
  • MCP server ships for Claude, Cursor, and Continue.
  • No API keys required; the real CISA KEV catalog is loaded minutes after boot.
  • Alerts show the originating connector; automated triage displays the local model’s verdict, confidence, and rationale verbatim.

🚀 Availability & Installation

Method Command
Windows PowerShell `iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beenuar/AiSOC/main/install.ps1
Linux/macOS curl `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beenuar/AiSOC/main/install.sh
Offline demo (no Docker) pip install aisoc-sandbox && aisoc-sandbox demo
  • Docker‑Compose v2 is optional; requires 8 GB memory, 20 GB free disk, Python 3.9+, and Bash.
  • make doctor validates the environment; make up creates .env with fifteen generated secrets and prints a one‑time admin password.
  • make clean removes the ~2 GB model volume; make bootstrap ARGS=--reset-password regenerates a lost admin password.
  • Ports already in use are detected, reported, and the install proceeds, publishing a new free port and moving the console address.
  • make smoke posts a real event through Kafka, detection, correlation, and Postgres to demonstrate end‑to‑end operation.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a fully auditable AI decision path, addressing trust concerns in automated security workflows.
  • Eliminates dependence on external API keys, enhancing privacy and reducing cost.
  • Offers a turnkey, self‑hosted solution that can run on a single server or via GitHub Codespaces.
  • Enables rapid threat‑intelligence updates and re‑analysis of historic data without vendor involvement.

#AISEC #OpenSource #Cybersecurity #LLM

Source: beenuar/AiSOC

item.title: SOCRadar Alerts Integration Brings External Threat Intel into Elastic Security
item.description:
SOCRadar Alerts Integration Brings External Threat Intel into Elastic Security

Your SOC runs on Elastic. Detections, logs, cases and dashboards all live in Kibana, and your analysts have built their muscle memory around it. Until now, external threat intelligence – alarms about the Surface, Deep and Dark Web, brand abuse or the external attack surface – arrived in a dedicated platform, were reviewed there, and then manually re‑keyed into the SIEM or case tool. The new SOCRadar Alerts integration (v0.1.0) eliminates that handoff.

🔎 Overview

  • The integration pulls SOCRadar alarms via the SOCRadar API on a configurable polling interval, with an initial historical look‑back to backfill recent alarms.
  • Each alarm arrives with severity, status, alarm type, sub‑type, affected asset, related entities and detailed information.
  • Alarm data is mapped to the Elastic Common Schema (ECS), so SOCRadar fields sit next to your other sources with consistent names.

🧩 How it works

  1. Polling – The integration queries the SOCRadar API on the schedule you set.
  2. Normalization – Incoming alarm fields are translated into ECS fields.
  3. Ingestion – Normalized alarm documents are stored in the same Elastic workspace used for internal telemetry.
  4. Visualization – A built‑in Kibana dashboard displays severity distribution, alarm categories, volume trends and recent incidents.
  5. Investigation – Analysts can pivot from a dashboard tile to the underlying alarm document, correlate it with endpoint or identity events, and open a case without leaving Kibana.

⚙️ Key details

  • Alarm attributes – Every alarm carries:
    • Severity
    • Status
    • Alarm type and sub‑type
    • Affected asset
    • Related entities
    • Detailed description
  • Analyst workflow – Search, filter and build rules on external alarms exactly as on internal telemetry; prioritize by severity across both.
  • Time saved – No manual copy‑paste between consoles; the external context that triggered the investigation is already in the case.
Attribute What it provides
Severity A severity level for prioritization
Status Current processing state of the alarm
Alarm type / sub‑type Classification of the finding
Affected asset The asset the alarm relates to
Related entities Additional objects linked to the alarm
Details Full description and context

🚀 Availability

  • The integration is listed in the Elastic integrations catalog. To enable it, open the catalog, search for SOCRadar, and add the SOCRadar Alerts integration with your SOCRadar API credentials and polling preferences.
  • If you are not yet a SOCRadar customer, or need help configuring the three integrations together, contact your SOCRadar customer success manager or request a demo.

💡 Why it matters

  • Unified workspace – External threat intelligence appears in the same Elastic Security workspace where analysts already work.
  • Reduced handoff – The costly manual step of re‑keying alarms is removed, eliminating bottlenecks caused by volume and lost context.
  • Actionable context – Each alarm includes the asset and related entities, so investigations start with concrete, validated information.
  • Continuous visibility – The built‑in Kibana dashboard gives immediate insight into spikes, such as a high‑severity “New Digital Asset Discovery” followed by an “Impersonating Domain” alarm, enabling rapid response.

#SOCRadar #ElasticSecurity #ThreatIntelligence #SIEM #ECS

Source: SOCRadar Alarms in Elastic | Investigate Threats Faster
